title: Different Models for Hawker Centre Management
what_it_is: Different Models for Hawker Centre Management

sections.label: Vacant stalls and Incubation Stall Programme
sections.summary: Questions ask the number of vacant NEA hawker stalls, take-up rate after floor price removal, and Incubation Stall Programme participation and continuation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what is the total number of vacant stalls at NEA-run hawker centres and markets as at 30 September 2018; and (b) what has been the take-up rate of vacant stalls since NEA removed the floor price.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how many hawkers have taken part in the Incubation Stall Programme; (b) how many will be continuing beyond the incubation period; and (c) for those who will not continue, what are the reasons and how will the Ministry address them.

sections.label: Hawker stall rentals and cap
sections.summary: Questions ask how many hawker stalls pay $10,000 or more monthly, the highest rental, and whether a rental cap will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how many hawker stalls are paying a rental of $10,000 or more per month; (b) what is the current highest rental that a hawker stall is paying; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider implementing a cap on the rental to better manage food prices.

sections.label: Social enterprise hawker centre costs
sections.summary: Questions cover rent and ancillary charges, cost structures, implicit subsidies, NEA plans, stock-take findings, and UNESCO bid effects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether rent and all ancillary charges payable by hawkers in hawker centres operated by not-for-profit social enterprises, such as dishwashing charges, are lower than those in NEA-managed hawker centres; and (b) if not, whether the Government intends to take any corrective action to reduce any additional business costs for the hawkers accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what is the relative cost structure of hawker stalls under NEA management, social enterprise management, and for-profit coffee shops respectively; (b) what are the nature and extent of implicit subsidies provided in NEA-managed hawker centres; and (c) whether the Ministry has plans for subsidising the operating costs of hawkers when hawkers experience difficulties in providing affordable food while earning a reasonable income.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how does NEA intend to help mitigate the cost increase in rental for the social enterprise-run hawker centres over time; and (b) whether NEA has any plans to run the hawker centres currently operated by social enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how long will NEA take to complete the stock-take of the social enterprise model of hawker centres; (b) whether the findings will be published for public consultation; and (c) whether the ongoing debate on social enterprise-run hawker centres will affect Singapore's bid for hawker culture to be listed under the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Yes, I will cover Question Nos 1 to 8 and Senior Minister of State Amy Khor will cover the rest.

sections.label: Building 20 new hawker centres
sections.summary: The Government committed to building 20 new hawker centres by 2027 in new or underserved estates, each costing $15 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Government has committed to building 20 new hawker centres by 2027 in new estates or existing ones that are relatively underserved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Each hawker centre costs $15 million to build.

sections.label: Ageing hawkers and retirement
sections.summary: The median hawker age is about 60, with about 6,000 cooked food stalls at 114 hawker centres and over one third retiring in 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Today, the median age of our hawkers is about 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have about 6,000 cooked food stalls at our 114 hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: More than one third of our hawkers and their assistants will retire in the next 10 years.

sections.label: Fixed rentals and operating costs
sections.summary: Operators must propose rentals and operating costs upfront and cannot change these over the tenancy term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Operators are required to propose rentals and operating costs upfront and cannot change these over the term of the tenancy.

sections.label: Operator surplus reinvestment requirement
sections.summary: Operators must reinvest at least 50% of any operating surplus into social benefits for hawker centres and stallholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Fourth, operators are required to reinvest at least 50% of any operating surplus into social benefits for the hawker centres and stallholders.

sections.label: Affordable meal option and pricing
sections.summary: Operators have made at least one affordable meal option at $3 and below available for each stall, and allowed hawkers to set other prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Instead, the operators have made available at least one affordable meal option at $3 and below for each stall and allowed hawkers to determine prices for other dishes.

sections.label: Hawker contract renewal rate
sections.summary: Hawkers are doing well and 97% of them chose to renew their contracts in July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The hawkers are doing well and 97% of them chose to renew their contracts in July this year.

sections.label: SEHC hawker age and training
sections.summary: The median age of hawkers at the seven SEHCs is 43, and the five SEHC operators have trained 38 aspiring hawkers since starting operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The median age of hawkers at the seven SEHCs is 43, significantly lower than the median 60 at our existing centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Collectively, the five SEHC operators have trained a total of 38 aspiring hawkers since they started operations.

sections.label: SEHC stall vacancy rate
sections.summary: Average monthly stall vacancy at SEHCs is about 10%, which is not exceptionally high and not a bad result given most stalls are new.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Overall, the average monthly stall vacancy at SEHCs, at about 10%, is not exceptionally high and is not a bad result, considering that most stalls are new.

sections.label: Adjusting and continuing SEHC model
sections.summary: The model will be adjusted to better serve Singaporeans, and the SEHC model will continue and be improved to serve patrons and look after hawkers' well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have heard the feedback and will adjust the model to better serve Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We will continue with the SEHC model and improve it so as to serve patrons well and look after the well-being of our hawkers.

sections.label: Hawker food price study findings
sections.summary: A 2014 study by the Ministry and MTI found raw materials and manpower were 76% of hawker costs, stall rentals 12%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: My Ministry, together with the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), conducted a study on the drivers of hawker centre food prices in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We found that the costs of raw materials and manpower made up the bulk of the hawkers' costs at 76%, not stall rentals, which only comprised 12%.

sections.label: Median SEHC stall rental
sections.summary: The median rental of stalls in SEHCs is about $2,000 per month, not $4,000 as some media reports claimed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The median rental of stalls in SEHCs is about $2,000 per month, not $4,000 per month as some media reports have claimed.

sections.label: New centre stall rentals
sections.summary: Actual stall rentals at new centres range from $750 to $3,700 a month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Additionally, the actual stall rentals at our new centres range from $750 to $3,700 a month.

sections.label: PHC grants extended to hawkers
sections.summary: PHC grants will be extended to SEHC hawkers for two years, effective from 1 January next year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Nonetheless, to further help SEHC stallholders manage costs, we announced last week that we will extend the PHC grants to these hawkers for two years, effective from 1 January next year.

sections.label: Stallholder working hours limits
sections.summary: Stallholders will not be required to work more than five days a week or eight hours a day, though they may.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Stallholders will not be required to work more than five days a week or eight hours a day, although they could if they wish to.

sections.label: Operator tenancy and breach limits
sections.summary: Operators cannot require over two months' notice or deposits above two months' rental, and liquidated damages are capped at $50 or $100 per day.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Operators will not require a notice period of more than two months for stallholders to terminate their tenancies or require security deposits exceeding two months’ rental.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Operators who impose liquidated damages on stallholders for regulatory or other breaches will limit these payments to no more than $50 per day for minor ones and $100 per day for major breaches.

sections.label: Hawkers can exit 24-hour operations
sections.summary: Hawkers who previously signed up for 24-hour operations may now stop them after operating hours changes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With the changes made to operating hours, hawkers who do not wish to continue with the 24-hour operations which they had previously signed up for, can do so now.

sections.label: Operator costs and surplus limits
sections.summary: Operators bear initiative costs, must plough back 50% of surplus, and face tender and rental limits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, many of these operators have been bearing the cost of various initiatives to improve footfall at the centres, such as free shuttle bus services and free parking not long after the centres began operations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: They are required under the terms of our tender to plough back at least 50% of any operating surplus for the social benefits of the hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This, plus our tender process which favours operators who charge lower total rental and operating costs and our prohibition on SEHC operators to increase any rental or operating costs over the tenancy period, limits the extent of any operating surplus.

sections.label: Possible penalties for operators
sections.summary: Potential measures include imposing liquidated damages or terminating operators' contracts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Potential measures include imposing liquidated damages, or even termination of their contracts.

sections.label: Nominating hawker culture for UNESCO
sections.summary: Next year, hawker culture is being nominated for the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Next year, we are nominating hawker culture for inscription on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

sections.label: Hawker centres as community dining rooms
sections.summary: Hawker centres are an important part of living culture and will thrive as community dining rooms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Our hawker centres should not be treated as nice-to-have dining options, but an important part of our living and evolving culture as, after all, we started building new hawker centres again because of the many appeals from the community for the hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I am confident that our hawker centres will continue to thrive as community dining rooms, bringing together Singaporeans from all walks of life and strengthening our bonds as a country.

sections.label: PHC Grant and surplus sharing terms
sections.summary: PHC Grant deducts CDW costs for hawkers, and operators must plough back at least 50% of surplus with NEA approval.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For the PHC Grant of 50% and 30% for first and second year respectively, these would directly benefit the hawkers, because 50% of the cost of the CDW will be deducted from the payment they have to make for the CDW.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Regarding the sharing of any operating surplus, it is in the terms of the tender agreement with the operator that, firstly, if they are not a social enterprise, they would have to set up a separate entity to tender for the hawker centre because we require them to submit an annual set of audited accounts to us.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And if there are any operating surplus, the condition is that they have to plough at least 50% of this operating surplus back to benefit the hawker centre, the hawkers or the community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Some of the proposals that have been made by the successful tenderers are, for instance, providing meal vouchers for needy residents or the elderly within the community, or sharing some of this operating surplus with the hawkers in terms of providing discounted meal vouchers or one-for-one meal vouchers, for instance, like Yishun Timbre+ does, to give to the residents so that they can purchase and part of the meal would be funded from the operating surplus.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Or it could be the training of hawkers or helping the low-income, for instance, to set up a hawker stall there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But if there is an operating surplus, they will have to propose how they want to plough this benefit back into the community or the hawker centre, and it would be subject to NEA's approval.

sections.label: Operator rentals and operating surplus
sections.summary: Operators offering lower rentals and operating costs cannot raise them during the tenancy, and any operating surplus must be ploughed back for social benefits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For instance, we favour operators who offer lower rentals and total operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: They cannot raise these rentals and operating costs through the term of the tenancy agreement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said, there is also the requirement to plough back any operating surplus for social benefits to the hawker centres, the hawkers and the community.

sections.label: Pre-fitted stalls trial offer
sections.summary: Stalls are offered subject to conditions, allowing rental of pre-fitted stalls for six months at 50% of assessed market rent to try out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we offered these stalls to them, subject to certain conditions, of course.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: They can rent these pre-fitted stalls for six months at 50% of the assessed market rent, and that is to allow them to try out.

sections.label: Incubation stalls and hawker models
sections.summary: Ten stalls are taken up with remaining incubation stalls being processed, complementing training programmes, and NEA is open to any model meeting social objectives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Ten stalls have been taken up and we have a list of applicants now which we are processing to lease out the remaining incubation stalls.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This actually complements the Entrepreneurship Programme and the Place and Train Programmes offered by the SEHC operators because many of the operators also offer training and entrepreneurship programmes for new hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Ci Yuan, for instance, trained 16 aspiring hawkers and 10 are still in Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, and they have converted to permanent hawkers and are doing well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Is NEA open to other models as well, such as, for example, Management Corporation Stata Title (MCST)-type, where the hawkers can come together to self-manage, or for NEA to still run the new hawker centres at least for a while and then transiting to the non-NEA-run model?

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I think we are open to any model as long as it is able to achieve the social objectives that we have set up for our new hawker centres, which is about providing affordable food options, moderating food prices, ensuring that the hawkers make a decent living and building communities.

sections.label: Contract change on operating days
sections.summary: Contracts with operators have been changed so that they need not open more than five days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First of all, let me say that we have actually worked with our operators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, now, one of the key changes we have made to the contracts is that they need not open more than five days.

sections.label: Construction and maintenance costs not recovered
sections.summary: For existing and new hawker centres, construction, upgrading and maintenance costs are not recovered through rentals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First, let me explain that for both our existing hawker centres and our new centres, the construction costs of the hawker centres, as well as the cost of upgrading and maintaining the hawker centres are not recovered through the rentals.

sections.label: Dishwashing cost comparison
sections.summary: Dishwashing costs appear lower in existing hawker centres because most lack CDWs, but with a CDW system essential costs are similar.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For dishwashing, what you see, for instance, when you compare, some people will say, "How come it is much lower in the existing hawker centres?" That is because of the cost element of dishwashing is often not taken into account in the existing hawker centres since most of the existing centres do not have CDWs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But if you were to take that in, you have to employ somebody for say, $1,500, just to wash dishes, or if the existing hawker centre has a CDW system, then the essential costs are actually quite similar.

sections.label: Hawker centre rentals and food prices
sections.summary: New hawker centre median rental is about $2,000 net of operating cost, and at least one affordable food option is required.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The range of $4,000 to $13,000 is, based on our survey, the rentals for coffee shops and food courts, not hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The rentals for our new hawker centres, median rental, is about $2,000, net of operating cost.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I have said earlier, what we are asking is that, to achieve our social objectives of offering affordable food prices as well as moderating food prices in the vicinity, at least one food option which is affordable, and most of these new centres have put that at about $3.00 or $2.80.

sections.label: Hawker centre operating surplus rules
sections.summary: At least 50% of surplus must go to social benefits, and new hawker centres with audited accounts had no accumulated operating surplus.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to the 50% surplus, at least 50% must go back to social benefits, the other 50%, of course, they can keep.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But so far, for our new hawker centres, those that have already submitted their audited accounts, none of them had accumulated any operating surplus.
